To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) group-affiliated firms tend to hold more cash than their stand-alone counterparts; and (b) the more diversified the group is, the more stock ownership holdings the group has, and the fewer listed firms the group has, the less cash the group-affiliated firms will hold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research questions: Do business groups affect the cash holdings of group-affiliated companies?
the relationship between business groups and corporate cash holdings.
the following questions: (1) Do business groups have a significant impact on group-affiliated firms' cash holdings decisions?

business group characteristics have a positive impact on group- affiliated firms cash holding.
the business groups in Taiwan have a negative relationship with group-affiliated firms' cash holdings, except group affiliation.

group-affiliated cash holdings are positively associated with group affiliation, group diversity, group ownership holdings and group listed numbers, and negatively associated with firm size, firm age, firm profitability, and firm growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
business group characteristics have significant effects on the cash holdings of business group-affiliated firm.
business groups have a positive impact on corporate cash holdings.
business groups have significant effects on the corporate cash holdings of their group affiliates in Taiwan.
The main takeaway from our work is that
business group affiliation, group ownership holdings and group diversification have significant effects on group-affiliated firms' cash holdings.
the cash holdings of group-affiliated companies are significantly higher than those of non-affiliated companies.
